newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures end down but off lows in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures end down but off lows in Tokyo.

text.p: Key December Japanese government bond futures ended down but off their lows on Monday.
Selling was sparked by a news report in late afternoon saying Japan's Post Office Life Insurance Bureau had started to become cautious of buying JGBs, traders said.
The report quoted the Fund Management Division of the Post Office Life Insurance Bureau as saying: "We cannot help but become cautious of making additional purchases of instruments such as JGBs."
The December ended at 124.65, down slightly from Friday's 124.75.
Turnover was 27,655 contracts.
The December fell to the afternoon low of 124.50 after the release of the news report, but inched up from there towards the close.
JGBs were supported by a comment by a Bank of Japan official that more failures of Japanese financial institutions could not be ruled out, traders said.

Tadayo Honma, executive director at the BOJ said: "Further failures (of financial institutions) cannot be ruled out. Major Japanese banks will make arrangements to finish disposing of their bad loans problems within the next one or two years."
Honma was speaking at a symposium on the international banking system.
The Ministry of Finance will offer 10-year JGBs through an auction on Tuesday, a MOF official said on Monday.
Traders said the amount of the issue is expected to be around one trillion yen.
The coupon rate is likely to be set at a record low of 2.8 percent, compared with 2.9 percent in the previous auction, traders said.
A coupon rate of 2.8 percent would be unlikely to invite strong demand from investors, they said.

Investors have been reluctant to buy JGBs with even a 2.9 percent coupon rate, so a coupon rate of 2.8 percent would likely make them even more hesitant, a trader for a city bank's securities affiliate said.
Investors remained sidelined ahead of the BOJ's key "tankan" survey of corporate sentiment due on Wednesday, traders said.

Economists surveyed by Reuters forecast on average that the diffusion index (DI) for big manufacturers would come in at about minus three, up from minus seven in August, when the previous survey was done.

But Yo Ogiwara, a senior analyst in the bond research department at Nomura Securities Investment Trust Management Co Ltd, said forecasts for the November tankan may not be very accurate, as economists were unable to incorporate industrial production data for October in their forecast models.
Ogiwara also said the bond market may be more interested in how the economy looks in the months ahead than how it looks now.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.635 percent as of 0730 GMT, up from Friday's 2.625 percent.
--Masayuki Kitano, +81-3-5473-3748
